newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Buenaventura to enter oil business.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Buenaventura to enter oil business.

text.p: Peruvian gold and silver miner Cia de Minas Buenaventura S.A. will enter the oil business by teaming up with two United States firms, a company official said Tuesday.
"We have reached an agreement in principal...to explore oil lots in the country," Buenaventura General Mnager Roque Benavides told Reuters in an interview.
"The agreement was reached with our subsidiary Buenaventura Ingenieros. It's a good opportunity to invest and enter the business," he added.

Buenaventura is a partner of U.S.-based Newmont Mining Co in Peru's richest gold miner Cia Minera Yanacocha S.A. The company also recently absorbed its subsidiaries Cia de Minas Orcopampa S.A. and Cia de Minas Recuperadas S.A.
"With our oil partners we plan to invest some $3 million to explore in oil lot 85, close to the Aguaytia gas deposit in the central jungle," Benavides said.
According to Mines and Energy Ministry sources, Buenaventura Ingenieros is in the process of negotiating with state-owned oil firm Petroperu to secure the license to explore and develop lot 85.

"They would invest in drilling the first well at a cost of about $2.1 million and we will invest the rest," Benavides said. "We are not leaving our main line of action because this is a small investment. It is part of a natural resources development strategy."
